prompt: Complete SafeBox so that neither the array passed to the constructor nor the array returned by getValues() can be used to mutate the box's internal state -- make defensive copies in both directions.
explanation: Array variables hold references, so simply assigning this.values = values would let the caller keep a handle on the box's internal array. Arrays.copyOf (or clone()) creates a brand new array with the same contents, so the constructor snapshots the input and getValues() hands out a throwaway copy. Mutations on either side then affect only the copies, never the private state.
hints: Assigning an array parameter straight to a field copies only the REFERENCE -- both variables then point at the same array object.
java.util.Arrays.copyOf(source, source.length) (or source.clone()) produces an independent copy.
You need two copies: one when the array comes in through the constructor, and one every time getValues() hands an array out.
